explore.intro: Easy first-day wandering and a full free day, with most city options reachable on foot or by tram from Sorell Hotel Seefeld.

options.title: Old Town, Lindenhof & lakefront loop
options.description: Walk from Seefeld along the lake to Bellevue, cross into Niederdorf, climb to Lindenhof, then return by Fraumünster and Bürkliplatz. It is an excellent jet-lag-proof introduction with cafés everywhere.

options.title: Short Lake Zurich cruise
options.description: Board near Bürkliplatz for a round-trip lake cruise. This is the easiest option for anyone who wants Alpine views without committing to a long walk.

options.title: Bahnhofstrasse & Old Town treasure hunt
options.description: Mix Bahnhofstrasse’s polished Swiss shops with the smaller book, watch, vintage, and antique storefronts around Augustinergasse, Münstergasse, and Spiegelgasse.

options.title: Uetliberg panorama walk
options.description: Take the train to Uetliberg and walk to the summit viewpoint over Zurich, the lake, and the Alps. The summit section is manageable, while stronger walkers can continue along the ridge.

options.title: Swiss whisky and cocktail detour
options.description: Old Crow’s deep spirits list makes a good evening stop for the bourbon-and-whisky contingent. Treat this as a small-group mission rather than an all-family field trip.

options.title: Live jazz at Moods
options.description: Check the June program at Moods in Zürich-West. The neighborhood also works well for dinner and a walk beneath the railway arches.

explore.intro: Keep this one compact: the Bernina Express departure is fixed, so choose one substantial outing or combine two easy options near the hotel.

options.title: Lake St. Moritz circuit
options.description: A mostly level loop directly from Waldhaus am See, with broad views toward St. Moritz and the Engadin peaks. This is the safest choice for a relaxed train-day morning.

options.title: Muottas Muragl panorama
options.description: Ride the funicular to one of the Engadin’s great viewpoints, then take a short panorama walk or simply enjoy the terrace. Confirm the summer operating schedule before committing.

options.title: St. Moritz village & Via Serlas
options.description: Browse the compact town center, luxury storefronts, local confectioners, and Engadin specialty shops. Add coffee and a slice of Bündner nut tart for essential cultural research.

options.title: Engadin Museum
options.description: A focused look at traditional Engadin interiors, furniture, and regional life. It is a useful weather-proof option and small enough to fit before the train transfer.

options.title: Engadin golf sampler
options.description: The Engadin courses around Samedan and Zuoz are spectacular, but the time window is tight. This works only with an early reserved tee time and a firm return plan for the Bernina Express.

explore.intro: The western shore rewards splitting into smaller crews. Some options are walkable from the villa area; others are best saved for the day when a van is available.

options.title: Valle delle Cartiere
options.description: Walk into Toscolano’s dramatic old paper-mill valley, where industrial ruins sit beside the stream and wooded trail. Choose a short out-and-back or continue farther into the gorge.

options.title: Maderno ferry to Torri del Benaco
options.description: Cross the lake by ferry, browse Torri del Benaco’s lanes and waterfront, then return to Maderno. Confirm the current timetable and last practical return before leaving.

options.title: Golf Bogliaco
options.description: One of Italy’s oldest golf clubs, with an 18-hole course above the western shore. Reserve tee times and club rentals early; the non-golfers can pair this with Gargnano or a lakeside lunch.

options.title: Isola del Garda tour
options.description: Boat to the lake’s largest island for a guided visit through gardens and the neo-Gothic villa. Tours are scheduled and should be booked rather than treated as a spontaneous stop.

options.title: Il Vittoriale & Gardone Riviera
options.description: Explore Gabriele D’Annunzio’s wonderfully eccentric estate, gardens, amphitheater, aircraft, and ship. Check the amphitheater calendar because summer performances can turn this into an evening plan.

options.title: Salò promenade & shopping
options.description: A flexible wander along Salò’s elegant waterfront and Via San Carlo, with boutiques, specialty food shops, cafés, and occasional vintage finds. Good for mixed-speed groups.

options.title: Private lake afternoon
options.description: Rent a skippered boat for swimming coves and shoreline villages without managing ferry schedules. Ask for pickup near Maderno and build the route around the group’s preferred balance of swimming and aperitivo.

explore.intro: A full choose-your-own-Milan day. Most city options work by Metro or taxi from Sina De La Ville, so the group can divide and regroup for aperitivo.

options.title: Brera art, antiques & design walk
options.description: Walk through Brera’s galleries, design stores, vintage shops, and antique dealers around Via Madonnina and Via Fiori Chiari. Add the Pinacoteca for anyone who wants serious art.

options.title: Duomo rooftops before the crowds
options.description: Book an early timed entry for the cathedral terraces, steps or elevator depending on the group. The hotel is close enough to make this the easiest high-impact outing.

options.title: Quadrilatero della Moda
options.description: Explore Via Montenapoleone, Via della Spiga, and the surrounding fashion district. Even determined non-shoppers may enjoy the architecture, courtyards, and people watching.

options.title: Sforza Castle to Navigli walk
options.description: Start at Castello Sforzesco, cross Parco Sempione, then continue by transit or on foot toward Sant’Ambrogio and the canals. Trim the route whenever gelato consensus collapses.

options.title: Navigli aperitivo & wine bars
options.description: Stroll the canals before aperitivo, then choose a quieter wine bar on a side street or embrace the lively waterfront. Reserve dinner if the whole family plans to reunite here.

options.title: Wine cellar beneath Brera
options.description: N’Ombra de Vin occupies an atmospheric cellar near San Marco and offers a broad Italian wine list. It pairs naturally with the Brera shopping route.

options.title: Blue Note Milano
options.description: Check the June 27 program for a seated jazz-club night. Booking ahead is sensible, and show times may allow either dinner at the club or a separate meal beforehand.

days.dogFact: Airport detection dogs do not smell “bad stuff” as one single scent. They learn specific odor signatures and can pick them out even inside a very busy suitcase. Basically: elite-level baggage gossip.
The Berger Blanc Suisse became an official Swiss breed in 1991. Its family tree traces back to a white shepherd named Lobo, who moved from the United States to Switzerland in the 1970s.

days.dogFact: Barry, Switzerland’s most famous Alpine rescue dog, reportedly saved more than 40 travelers. He retired to Bern, and his preserved remains are still cared for by the city’s Natural History Museum.

days.dogFact: The word Sennenhund means “Alpine herdsman’s dog.” Switzerland has four famous Sennenhund breeds, all developed to move cattle, guard farms, and occasionally pull carts through mountain country.

days.dogFact: The iconic St. Bernard brandy barrel is mostly a painting-and-postcard myth. The real hospice dogs carried something better: powerful noses, warm bodies, and the ability to find travelers in deep Alpine snow.

days.dogFact: Italy’s Lagotto Romagnolo started as a water-retrieving dog before becoming the world’s best-known truffle hunter. “Lagotto” comes from a dialect word connected to lakes and wetland work.

events.notes: Pool, lake, and a slow afternoon

days.dogFact: Some wineries employ trained dogs to detect TCA, the compound behind “corked” wine. A good wine dog can inspect cellars and barrels without requesting even one tasting flight.

events.notes: One van plus ferry or taxi

days.dogFact: Plain cooked pasta is generally not toxic to dogs, but the sauce may be another story: onions and garlic are unsafe for them. The official canine pasta order is therefore “plain, tiny, and dropped accidentally.”
Verona’s celebrated medieval ruler Cangrande della Scala had an extremely dog-friendly name: Cangrande literally means “Big Dog.” His court helped make the city a major cultural center.

days.summary: A free day by the lake
days.dogFact: Dogs experience REM sleep and appear to dream. Researchers think the little paw twitches and muffled woofs may replay daily adventures, so today’s lake nap could become tonight’s imaginary boat chase.

days.summary: Lake Iseo en route to Milan
days.dogFact: The Bergamasco Shepherd comes from the Alpine country around Bergamo, near today’s route. Its famous felted coat forms naturally into protective mats that helped shield working dogs from mountain weather.

events.event: Check in at Sina De La Ville

days.dogFact: Italian Greyhounds were favorites of Renaissance nobility and appeared in art for centuries. Six of the modern breed’s early show dogs were exhibited in Milan and Novara in 1901. Tiny dog, enormous social résumé.

A dog’s nose can separate the individual ingredients in a mixed smell, which is why airport dogs can work amid coffee, perfume, luggage, and thousands of travelers. Meanwhile, humans can barely find Gate B12.
